primaryFeatures.name: Persistent Match Statistics

modules.lesson:
The document head is the brain of your webpage, containing metadata that tells the browser how to render your content, such as character encoding and viewport settings for mobile responsiveness. By linking an external stylesheet, you separate your visual design from your structural HTML, keeping your codebase clean and maintainable.

For example, to set the viewport, you use: <meta name='viewport' content='width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0'>.

modules.title: Core UI Elements & Interactive Controls
modules.learningObjective: Build the 3x3 button-based game grid and the statistical display footer.
modules.lesson:
Building a user interface for a game requires a clear structure that separates the game board from the supporting information. By using CSS Grid, we can easily create a responsive 3x3 layout for our cells, ensuring they maintain their shape and alignment regardless of the screen size. This approach keeps our HTML clean and our layout logic centralized in the stylesheet.

When working with interactive elements, remember that semantic HTML is your best friend. Using buttons for the game cells makes them naturally focusable and accessible. For example, you can style a button to look like a simple square: button { width: 50px; height: 50px; border: 1px solid #ccc; }.

modules.title: Core JavaScript Logic & Event Handling
modules.learningObjective: Create the game state loop, win condition checking, and event listeners for player moves.
modules.lesson:
In JavaScript, event handling allows us to respond to user interactions like clicks. By attaching listeners to DOM elements, we can trigger functions that update the application state and reflect those changes in the UI. This creates an interactive loop where the user input drives the game logic.

For example, you can listen for a click on a button like this: `document.querySelector('#my-btn').addEventListener('click', () => console.log('Clicked!'));`

modules.title: State Persistence / Reset & Final Integration
modules.learningObjective: Implement localStorage serialization to save player stats and hook up the game reset functionality.
modules.lesson:
State persistence allows your application to remember user data even after a page refresh. By using the Web Storage API, specifically localStorage, you can serialize JavaScript objects into JSON strings and store them in the browser's persistent memory. This is a fundamental technique for creating seamless user experiences in web applications.

For example, to save a user preference: `localStorage.setItem('theme', 'dark');`. To retrieve it: `const theme = localStorage.getItem('theme');`.
modules.task:
### Goal
Implement the `localStorage` logic to track wins and ties, and complete the `restartGame` function to reset the board state and UI.

### Requirements
- Implement `loadStats()` and `saveStats()` functions using `localStorage`.
- Update `checkWinner()` to call `saveStats()` and `updateStatsDisplay()`.
- Implement `restartGame()` to clear the board, reset `isGameActive`, and clear `statusText`.
- Ensure the `restart-btn` triggers the `restartGame` function.

### Example
```javascript
const data = { score: 10 };
localStorage.setItem('game', JSON.stringify(data));
```

### If you're stuck
Check the Hints and MDN references below for guidance on `JSON.stringify` and `localStorage` methods.

solutionFiles.content: const board = document.getElementById('game-board'); const cells = document.querySelectorAll('.cell'); const turnIndicator = document.getElementById('turn-indicator'); const statusText = document.getElementById('game-status'); const restartBtn = document.getElementById('restart-btn'); const xWinsEl = document.getElementById('x-wins'); const oWinsEl = document.getElementById('o-wins'); const tiesCountEl = document.getElementById('ties-count'); const STORAGE_KEY = 'tictactoe_stats_v1'; let currentPlayer = 'X'; let boardState = ['', '', '', '', '', '', '', '', '']; let isGameActive = true; let stats = { x: 0, o: 0, ties: 0 }; const winningConditions = [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5], [6, 7, 8], [0, 3, 6], [1, 4, 7], [2, 5, 8], [0, 4, 8], [2, 4, 6]]; function loadStats() { try { const saved = localStorage.getItem(STORAGE_KEY); if (saved) { stats = JSON.parse(saved); xWinsEl.textContent = stats.x; oWinsEl.textContent = stats.o; tiesCountEl.textContent = stats.ties; } } catch (e) { console.warn('Failed to load stats:', e); } } function saveStats() { try { localStorage.setItem(STORAGE_KEY, JSON.stringify(stats)); } catch (e) { console.warn('Failed to save stats:', e); } } function handleCellClick(e) { const cell = e.target; const index = parseInt(cell.dataset.index); if (boardState[index] !== '' || !isGameActive) return; boardState[index] = currentPlayer; cell.textContent = currentPlayer; cell.classList.add(currentPlayer.toLowerCase()); checkWinner(); } function checkWinner() { let roundWon = false; let winningLine = []; for (let i = 0; i < winningConditions.length; i++) { const [a, b, c] = winningConditions[i]; if (boardState[a] && boardState[a] === boardState[b] && boardState[a] === boardState[c]) { roundWon = true; winningLine = [a, b, c]; break; } } if (roundWon) { statusText.textContent = `Player ${currentPlayer} Wins!`; winningLine.forEach(idx => cells[idx].classList.add('win')); isGameActive = false; if (currentPlayer === 'X') stats.x++; else stats.o++; updateStatsDisplay(); saveStats(); return; } if (!boardState.includes('')) { statusText.textContent = 'Game Ended in a Draw!'; isGameActive = false; stats.ties++; updateStatsDisplay(); saveStats(); return; } currentPlayer = currentPlayer === 'X' ? 'O' : 'X'; turnIndicator.textContent = `Player ${currentPlayer}'s Turn`; turnIndicator.style.color = currentPlayer === 'X' ? 'var(--color-x)' : 'var(--color-o)'; } function updateStatsDisplay() { xWinsEl.textContent = stats.x; oWinsEl.textContent = stats.o; tiesCountEl.textContent = stats.ties; } function restartGame() { currentPlayer = 'X'; boardState = ['', '', '', '', '', '', '', '', '']; isGameActive = true; statusText.textContent = ''; turnIndicator.textContent = "Player X's Turn"; turnIndicator.style.color = 'var(--color-x)'; cells.forEach(cell => { cell.textContent = ''; cell.className = 'cell'; }); } cells.forEach(cell => cell.addEventListener('click', handleCellClick)); restartBtn.addEventListener('click', restartGame); loadStats();
